searchText: Question about 7702 and quantum: sooner or later all EOAs will need to either voluntarily or forcibly upgrade for quantum resistance. Won't EOAs set with code via 7702 get left behind and eventually cracked due to an inability to upgrade/rotate? I think maybe that's what VB was saying here: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/718596092828057631/1210414924375924796 Sorry I'm not as deep in this stuff as everyone else here, so I apologize if this has been addressed. 7702 allows users to more easily migrate all assets to a smart contract wallet if neccessary, but in a PQ world we almost certainly need a solution for turning off the EC crypto for accounts in which case that would avoid users from being cracked I'm trying to use 7702 to give many users access to do certain actions from a shared EOA (public private key) and lock down all other actions. In this odd case, we don't care if it's never upgradeable and cracked bc the key is already open. If there were ever a mass force-upgrade, the solution would be broken So how would this work with 7702? likely there would be a window of time where you can elect to upgrade to a PQ key pair and after that window EC crypto would be turned off so you wouldn’t need to do anything So that's confirmed that it would brick the EOA? That's no good How exactly would this work? What I need to know is: can the upgrade to a PQ key pair be disabled? That is, 7702 allows you to set up an EOA so that it can do X Y and Z but not A B and C. Is upgrading from EC to PQ crypto a "thing" 7702 can (or by default already does?) disallow? Or will upgrading *always* be available to someone with the private key? Simplified: (a) upgrading to PQ crypto will *never* be possible from a 7702 EOA (b) upgrading to PQ crypto will *always* be possible from a 7702 EOA (c) developer's choice. Upgrading to PQ crypto depends on the code set in the EOA by 7702 Which is the correct answer? (edit: assume all of these are before the old EC crypto is globally shut off) > can the upgrade to PQ key pair be disabled yes, just deploy a smart contract using normal methods 🙂 for EOAs, it does not seem likely that will be disabled i assume the answer will be b) before old EC crypto is turned off, but this has not been fully determined yet Do we have a sense for the flow of upgrading an EOA to PQ crypto? How will it actually work, in practice? my mental model is 1) there is a fork that allows EOA to add a PQ public key via a tx or possibly and opcode for 7702 accounts - this may or may not disable the EC key 2) a later fork will disable txs originating from accounts using an EC key

excerpts.author: fivedogit
excerpts.content:
What I need to know is: can the upgrade to a PQ key pair be disabled? 
That is, 7702 allows you to set up an EOA so that it can do X Y and Z but not A B and C. 
Is upgrading from EC to PQ crypto a "thing" 7702 can (or by default already does?) disallow?
Or will upgrading *always* be available to someone with the private key?

Simplified:
(a) upgrading to PQ crypto will *never* be possible from a 7702 EOA
(b) upgrading to PQ crypto will *always* be possible from a 7702 EOA
(c) developer's choice. Upgrading to PQ crypto depends on the code set in the EOA by 7702
Which is the correct answer? (edit: assume all of these are before the old EC crypto is globally shut off)

> can the upgrade to PQ key pair be disabled
yes, just deploy a smart contract using normal methods 🙂 for EOAs, it does not seem likely that will be disabled

i assume the answer will be b) before old EC crypto is turned off, but this has not been fully determined yet
